instruction: I am an NLP researcher downloading papers. Look up the ACL 2019, 2020, and 2021 best paper awards on the ACL Anthology website and add them to the table best_awards_acl.xlsx on the desktop. For each paper, include the title, year, author list (comma-separated), and the direct PDF download link from ACL Anthology (links should end with .pdf).

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Variation 9: Task asks to add 3 ACL best paper awards (2019, 2020, 2021) with title, year, authors, and PDF links. Evaluator extracts all paper data from columns A-D (title, year, authors, pdf_link) and verifies: (1) at least 3 papers are present with all required fields, (2) papers cover the required years (2019, 2020, 2021), (3) all PDF links contain 'aclanthology.org' and end with '.pdf', (4) all fields have meaningful content. Score is weighted: 60% for year coverage, 40% for paper validity.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Getter extracts all 4 required fields (title, year, authors, pdf_link) from columns A-D. Metric validates all fields are present and meaningful.
Year verification: Metric correctly checks that papers cover the required years (2019, 2020, 2021) and awards 60% of score based on year coverage.
Field validation: Metric validates meaningful content (title > 5 chars, authors > 3 chars, year present) and correct PDF link format (contains 'aclanthology.org', ends with '.pdf').
Reasonable partial credit: Weighted scoring (60% year coverage + 40% paper validity) appropriately rewards completing different aspects of the task.

Minor limitation: Cannot programmatically verify these are the actual 'best paper award' winners vs random ACL papers from those years. However, this is infeasible without a gold standard database and the current checks are reasonable proxies for task completion.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding title keyword checks if specific best paper award titles are known (e.g., checking for common award-winning paper title patterns).
Could add stricter year validation by checking year field matches exactly '2019', '2020', or '2021' rather than just containing the year string.
